AfterSideTurnEnd.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): The reset moved to the right slot. Kusarigama.cs's player-side AfterSideTurnEnd is turn_structure step 64, which runs AFTER the hand flush; the port used `on_player_turn_end`, which is Hook.BeforeTurnEnd (step 48) -- about sixteen steps too early. `relics/kusarigama.py` now implements `after_player_turn_end`, the slot whose own docstring names Hook.AfterTurnEnd and distinguishes it from BeforeTurnEnd. The reachability the entry established is what made it matter: the ported StampedePower auto-plays N Attacks from the LATER slot, so the counter was being cleared before those plays could count toward it.  Pinned by test/test_relic_residue_gaps.py.  NOT CLOSED: nothing at this site.  The text it replaced read: WRONG TURN-END SLOT. C#'s player-side AfterSideTurnEnd is audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json step 64 -- it runs AFTER the hand flush -- and the sim HAS that slot: hooks.after_player_turn_end (hooks.py:1267, renumbered since prior pass, content unchanged), whose own docstring says it is Hook.AfterTurnEnd and is 'Distinct from on_player_turn_end, which is Hook.BeforeTurnEnd' (step 48). kusarigama.py:32-33 uses on_player_turn_end, so the reset happens ~16 steps too early. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b08.py b08-kusarigama): the ported StampedePower auto-plays N Attacks from `on_player_turn_end` (powers.py:1023-1039) -- the SAME sim hook -- and its C# home is StampedePower.cs:18 AfterAutoPostPlayPhaseEntered, which turn_structure step 47 places BEFORE step 64. So C# always resets after those Attacks and the sim may not: with Stampede(2) on the player and the executed listener order ['Kusarigama', 'StampedePower'], end_turn leaves _attacks_this_turn=2 where C# leaves 0, and those 2 carry into the next turn -- shifting every 'every 3rd Attack' trigger for the rest of the combat. Both sides ported: Stampede is the Ironclad card cards/stampede.py:36. Bounded, not run-wide: the on_combat_start reset above stops it leaking past the combat. The `participants.Contains(base.Owner.Creature)` filter is structurally satisfied (the sim fires this hook for the player side only). Fix: move the reset to after_player_turn_end, the slot relics/parrying_shield.py:24 already uses. Rule 7: hooks.py, powers.py, cards/stampede.py, relics/parrying_shield.py, src/Core/Models/Powers/StampedePower.cs and audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: G2 (DORMANT): `Owner.Creature.CombatState.HittableEnemies` (Kusarigama.cs:115) vs the candidate-set helper the port calls
guards.issue: REVISED 2026-08-04: STALE against current code -- this guard's own premise ('the sim's living_enemies()') was already superseded by the fix the sibling `AfterCardPlayed` hook entry on this same record documents. `kusarigama.py:49` now calls `self.hittable_enemies()`, not `living_enemies()`, and `Relic.hittable_enemies()` (relics/base.py:495-497) now exists and delegates to `CombatState.hittable_enemies` (which itself mirrors `CombatState.HittableEnemies`, CombatState.cs:142, filtering on `!IsDead && Hook.ShouldAllowHitting`). What remains, and why the verdict stays `gap`/DORMANT rather than moving to `faithful`, is the same residual the hook entry already names: the fix is currently unobservable because every ported `should_allow_hitting` implementer (IllusionPower powers.py:1572-1575, AdaptablePower powers.py:3372-3375) only ever refuses a mid-revival creature, which cannot coexist with 'alive and un-gone' -- so `hittable_enemies() == living_enemies()` for every reachable state today. Porting any effect that makes a LIVING enemy untargetable makes it live, and in an RNG-visible way (the CombatTargets stream position stays equal but the chosen index diverges, since `combat_rng.targets.choice(...)` is Rng.NextItem scaled by len(seq), rng.py:248-252).
